author: f. e. graff
title: Hawaiʻi men's volleyball team rallies to defeat UC Irvine in five sets
text:
The University of Hawaiʻi men’s volleyball team won a close match against UC Irvine on April 3, coming back from a 2-1 deficit to secure a five-set victory (25-22, 19-25, 23-25, 25-23, 18-16) at the Bren Events Center.
This win keeps the Rainbow Warriors’ road record perfect at 8-0 and moves their Big West Conference record to 5-0 halfway through the conference schedule. The result also continues Hawaiʻi’s strong performance in Irvine, marking their tenth win in the last eleven matches played at the Bren Events Center.
Tread Rosenthal led Hawaiʻi with an all-around performance that included 53 assists, ten digs, nine kills, and six blocks. Kristian Titriyski contributed a team-high sixteen kills and two aces. Louis Sakanoko added fourteen kills while hitting .367 and made seven digs. Adrien Roure recorded twelve kills and eleven digs for his first double-double of the season. Trevell Jordan was efficient in the middle with twelve kills on sixteen swings without an error (.750 hitting percentage) along with four blocks.
The match saw both teams trading momentum throughout each set. After taking the first set, Hawaiʻi dropped the next two but responded by winning sets four and five under pressure. The decisive fifth set featured several lead changes before Hawaiʻi clinched victory on their fourth match point following a UC Irvine attack error.
UC Irvine was led by Andrej Jokanovic with twenty-two kills and William D’Arcy with fourteen kills. The Anteaters hit .304 as a team compared to .325 for Hawaiʻi.
Hawaiʻi will face UC Irvine again in a rematch scheduled for Saturday evening at the same venue.
